profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Seattle, a two-part data center campus in Tukwila, King County, Washington, marketed by the operator as the West Coast's largest privately owned data center campus. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in this same Tukwila location became SDC Seattle Building 5, prompting Sabey's pivot into the data center industry. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Seattle page, the Tukwila campus totals more than a million square feet and 54 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure not broken out per individual building and not applied to any single structure here. Aggregator sourcing indicates the campus actually comprises two separately addressed sub-campuses: Intergate.East, at a street range of 3311 to 3511 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168, spanning roughly 1.2 million square feet; and Intergate.West, at 12101 to 12301 Tukwila International Boulevard, Tukwila, WA 98168, built in 1999 and spanning roughly 173,000 square feet.

This building, Intergate.East Building 5, is per the operator's own site the very building whose vacated tenant space originally became Sabey's first data center in the early 2000s, prompting the company's pivot into the data center industry from its prior business as a commercial real estate developer. Aggregator DatacenterHawk lists this building at 3355 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168; aggregator DC Hub independently places the building at the same general Tukwila coordinates without offering its own street address.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 54 MW (operator figure) across the Tukwila campus, not applied to this individual building.
profile.research_note: Gap-view review: Sabey publishes SDC Seattle only as a campus-wide total (1M+ sqft / 54MW across Intergate.East + Intergate.West sub-campuses), not broken out per building. No per-building figure exists for Intergate.East Building 5 (Sabey's original data center building). No numeric key written.

reading.body:
Sabey Data Centers operates Intergate Seattle East Building 5 as part of its two-building Tukwila campus, which publishes 54 MW of total capacity across roughly 1.2 million square feet at the East sub-campus and 173,000 square feet at the West sub-campus. The operator does not publish a power figure for this individual building, making its AI hosting potential impossible to quantify from available data. This is the structure that originated Sabey's data center business in the early 2000s when a vacated tenant space prompted the company's pivot from commercial real estate development.

The campus holds SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 1 Type 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and HITECH certifications, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in healthcare, payments, and information security. It also holds LEED Gold certification. None of these certifications indicate whether the facility currently hosts AI training, inference, or other accelerator workloads.

At the campus level, Sabey's 54 MW published capacity ranks third among Washington state's two facilities with published power figures, though Washington state has 46 mapped data center locations whose individual capacities remain unpublished. Without a per-building breakdown, Intergate.East Building 5 cannot be evaluated independently as a constraint on AI scaling in the region.
